calls.head: Stützle gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Flyers keep sending Dvorak’s line (Dvorak, Foerster and Barkey) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Tocchet has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Senators’ first line is Batherson, Stützle and Halliday.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 38% chance, and they proved us wrong.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 62% chance, but Philadelphia had other ideas.

surprises.head: Philadelphia couldn’t get good looks
surprises.body: Philadelphia usually gets worse looks than most teams, and Ottawa usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Philadelphia’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 2.9% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 350 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: At last, a first win for the Flyers
paras: The Flyers won for the first time this season, at the tenth try, after starting 0-6-3. Drake Batherson got the scoring started for the Senators early in the second, but they didn’t score again. Porter Martone tied it 1-1 for Philadelphia just over three minutes later, and Matvei Michkov put the Flyers ahead for good on the power play late in the period. The Sens’ Thomas Chabot left later in the period and didn’t return. Trevor Zegras added the empty-netter with 14 seconds left to make it 3-1.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. Dan Vladař made 25 saves for the Flyers, and Linus Ullmark stopped 25 of 27. The Flyers improved to 1-6-3, and the Senators dropped to 6-3-0.

items.text: Drake Batherson passed Radek Bonk for ninth on the Senators’ all-time goals list, with 153.

The season series is even at 1-1.
